title: Lower cardinality estimate for substring/LIKE table filters
summary: I changed `RelationStatisticsHelper::ExtractGetStats` in `src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp` (only that `.cpp` file, no header change). If a non-optional table filter is a string pattern match against a constant, the default selectivity drops from 0.2 to 0.05. This covers an ExpressionFilter, or one inside a ConjunctionAndFilter, whose BoundFunctionExpression is `contains`, `like`, `~~`, `ilike`, `~~*`, `like_escape`, `ilike_escape`, `regexp_matches`, `suffix` or `ends_with`, with a constant second argument. The new constant `STRING_PATTERN_SELECTIVITY` is a file-local constexpr. Equality-filter estimates still take precedence, and every other filter behaves exactly as before. The release build passes. q09.m0 EXPLAIN ANALYZE went from 1.39s to 1.03s. The plan now joins partsupp to the filtered part table first (436K rows), then joins lineitem on both keys while building on that small side. The orders join builds on the 3.27M intermediate, not on the 15M orders scan. Bench result: q09 went from 980.7 ms to 723.0 ms (-26.3%), and the geomean also fell 26.3%. Result checks passed.
notes: Follow-up: in the new plan the lineitem scan no longer gets the dynamic bloom filter on its part key (`IN BF(p_partkey)`). It now reads all 60M rows (2.16s of scan time) instead of 3.45M, and the 2-key join takes 2.38s of operator time. The old plan had the part table as a direct build child of the lineitem join, so its bloom filter was pushed into the scan. Now the build side is partsupp⋈part, and the dynamic filter only carries min/max bounds, not a bloom filter. Two ways to get a further large gain: let bloom-filter pushdown work when the build side is a join whose output still covers the key, or have the join order prefer joining lineitem to part directly. I did not try either, to keep this diff small. Also, the 2-key join estimate counting only one key, which the issue raised, did not block the flip here.

title: Bloom filter pushdown for multi-key hash joins on the first key
summary:
I allowed the hash-join bloom filter to be pushed down for multi-key equi-joins, on the first join condition only. The tree builds in release, and bench on q09 went from 723.1ms to 536.1ms (-25.9%) with results matching the current best.

Changes:
(1) physical_hash_join.cpp, CanUseBloomFilter: the `conditions.size()==1` requirement is gone. It now requires that both the pushed condition and ht->conditions[0] are COMPARE_EQUAL. FinalizeFilters only calls it when join_condition[filter_idx]==0. The other existing checks are unchanged: has_cast, perfect HT, build_side_has_filter, probe larger than build.
(2) join_hashtable.cpp: InsertHashes now only feeds the stored row hashes into the bloom filter for single-key tables. For multi-key tables, Finalize gathers key column 0 from the row locations per chunk with data_collection->Gather(..., column 0, ...), hashes it with VectorOperations::Hash and inserts those hashes. That is the same hash BFTableFilter computes on the probe side. The hash table never probes the bloom filter itself, so the combined row hash is not needed anywhere else. No header changes.

Profile of q09.m0: the lineitem scan now shows `l_partkey IN BF(p_partkey)` and emits 3.28M rows instead of 60M. The 2-key HASH_JOIN dropped from 2.27s to 0.65s. The scan's own time went up (3.37s in the profile), because it now evaluates the bloom filter.

Correctness checks I ran with dbe-tool sql:
- A 3-key join with a VARCHAR first key (lineitem self-join on shipinstruct, suppkey, linenumber against a filtered DISTINCT build) returned 554655, the same as the equivalent join on concatenated string keys.
- A 2-key integer join against a filtered partsupp returned 295319, the same as the concatenated-key version.

Two other VARCHAR attempts returned 0 rows on both sides, so they test nothing. I did not specifically test NULL first keys or the external/spilling hash join.
notes:
- After this change the q09 lineitem scan (about 3.4s cumulative in the profile) is the dominant cost. The next idea is to push the bloom filter for the second key (suppkey) as well. That would need a separate BloomFilter member per condition, which is a header change.
- Inside the 2-key bloom filter, the min/max filters on l_suppkey do nothing.
- For external (partitioned) joins the bloom filter lifecycle is the same as the existing single-key path; this change only alters which hashes are inserted. I did not test that path specifically.

title: Software prefetch of hash-table entries and rows in hash join probe
reasons: no visible template faster beyond its noise (best: q09 -4.7%; needs at least -5%)
summary: Added software prefetching to the hash-join paths in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp. Prefetching is only a hint and the logic is unchanged, so results are identical. (1) In ProbeForPointersInternal, before the main loop, a pass prefetches entries[hashes_dense[i] & bitmask] for every probe row. (2) In GetRowPointersInternal, before row_matcher_build.Match, a pass prefetches the row pointers for keys_to_compare_sel. (3) In InsertHashesLoop, before each probing round, the target entries are prefetched for writing. All three are guarded by GCC/Clang and run only when capacity*sizeof(ht_entry_t) is above a fixed 1MB (L2-scale) constant. The build passes and results check out. Bench on q09 against the current best, four runs: -5.7% and -4.8% with probe prefetch only (1)+(2); then -9.9% and -5.6% after adding the build prefetch (3).
notes: The gain is real but modest (about 5-10% on q09) and close to the noise bar. Out-of-order execution apparently already overlaps some of the misses. Prefetching for the whole vector at once is crude: it issues up to 2048 prefetches, more than the hardware can keep in flight. A possible next step is distance-based prefetching inside the loop (prefetch i+16 while processing i), which could do better. The build-side prefetch added visible gain, so the build phase matters for q09 as well. A separate idea that was not tried: prefetching chained rows in ScanStructure::Next/AdvancePointers for chains longer than one.

title: Hash join prefetch v2: build insert + probe, software-pipelined, LLC-sized threshold
summary:
I added software prefetching to the hash join, all in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp. q09 ran -12.9% (514.9 → 448.7 ms) and then -14.6% (520.3 → 444.2 ms) in two benches against the current best. Both benches also checked results, and they matched.

The changes:
(a) Two file-local helpers, PrefetchRead and PrefetchWrite, which wrap __builtin_prefetch under GCC/Clang and do nothing on other compilers. A prefetch distance of 16. A gate, ShouldPrefetch(ht), that is true only when capacity*sizeof(ht_entry_t) is over 4MB.
(b) ProbeForPointersInternal takes a new template parameter, PREFETCH, chosen once per call in ProbeForPointers. When it is set, iteration i prefetches entries[hashes_dense[i+16] & bitmask]. The non-prefetch version is the same code as before.
(c) GetRowPointersInternal: when the gate is on, a short loop prefetches the build-row pointers for keys_to_compare_sel before row_matcher_build.Match.
(d) InsertHashesLoop (the build): when the gate is on, each insert iteration prefetches, for write, the entry 16 positions ahead in remaining_sel.
(e) ScanStructure::AdvancePointers: after following a chain pointer that isn't null, it prefetches the next row. This code only runs when chains_longer_than_one is set.

There are no header changes and no change in behaviour, since a prefetch is only a hint.
notes: The gain was much larger than E0003 measured (-13% to -15% vs about -5%). That supports the idea that prefetching a fixed distance ahead inside the loops, with build and probe together, beats a 2048-wide pre-pass. I did not test each part on its own, so I don't know how much each one contributes. I also did not test other distances (8 or 32) or other thresholds. A possible follow-up is prefetching the hash-table entry again in the linear-probe retry loop that runs after key mismatches. That loop is rare, so it is probably minor.

title: Bitpacking select: decode only the selected rows' blocks for filtered scans
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary: I added `BitpackingSelect<T>` to src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp and registered it with `bitpacking.select = BitpackingSelect<T>`. It walks metadata groups and 32-value algorithm groups the same way BitpackingScanPartial does and keeps a cursor into the ascending selection vector. FOR blocks with no selected row are skipped without unpacking. DELTA_FOR blocks are always unpacked and delta-decoded so the delta chain stays intact, and CONSTANT / CONSTANT_DELTA values are computed directly. Only the selected values are written, into a compact flat vector. If more than 75% of rows are selected, it falls back to a full scan followed by in-place compaction. It builds (BUILD OK). A temporary debug throw confirmed the callback runs on the q09 lineitem scan, where the validity columns use Constant compression, which supports select. Benchmark results for q09 (SF10, about 450-480 ms): -0.0%, +7.5% (noise), +0.1%. There is no measurable gain, so I'm abandoning. I didn't run the planned correctness matrix (selectivities, NULLs, DELTA_FOR boundaries) because the change shows no effect.
notes: The hypothesis's cost estimate does not hold for hot runs. One-shot EXPLAIN ANALYZE through `dbe-tool sql` (a cold process each time) shows the lineitem scan at 3.78 s CPU with 5 extra columns versus 0.86 s with only l_partkey. That gap is cold buffer and IO cost (pinning and reading pages), not decode, and hot bench numbers did not move at all with sparse decode. Future planners should estimate per-column scan costs from hot runs (bench/profile), not from single `dbe-tool sql` timings. The q09 profile shows the o_orderkey = l_orderkey HASH_JOIN at 1.50 s CPU and the lineitem TABLE_SCAN at 3.70 s; the time inside the scan is probably dominated by the BF filter on l_partkey and buffer handling, not by decoding the non-filter columns. Side observation: BitpackingScanPartial's CONSTANT branch fills `remaining` elements instead of `to_scan` (an existing quirk, harmless because the next group overwrites them).

title: Hash join prefetch distance tuning (16 -> 32) plus prefetch on the probe-retry path
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary: Changed HT_PREFETCH_DISTANCE in src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp, which sets the distance for both the probe and build-insert loops. Timed q09 against the current best (distance 16). Distance 32 over three runs: -2.7%, +9.1%, -7.6%, a mean of about -0.4%. Distance 64 over one run: +6.7%. The quick bench's spread here is about ±9%, so 32 is indistinguishable from 16 and 64 looks worse. In the profile at distance 32, the o_orderkey=l_orderkey HASH_JOIN took 1.43s, against 1.31s in .dbe/profile.md at distance 16. That is no improvement, though the two numbers come from different runs. Nothing came close to the 5% bar, so the tree is left as is.
notes: Prefetch distance tuning is a dead end: 16 to 32 shows no measurable gain, and 64 looks slower, probably from line-fill-buffer pressure or prefetched lines being evicted before use. I didn't try 48 or separate probe and build distances, since 32 showed nothing. In the profile the orders join is the probe side: 15M orders rows probe a hash table built from the 3.27M lineitem rows that survive the earlier joins. The time there is not only probe latency; it also includes the 15M-row scan feeding it and the hashing. A better lever is probably to cut the 15M probe rows before they reach the join: push a bloom filter or min/max filter from the lineitem-side build keys into the orders scan. Only 3.27M of 15M rows match, so a filter on the build keys should drop about 78% of probes. The dynamic filters listed on the orders scan show none on o_orderkey. That likely comes down to the E0002 bloom pushdown not firing for this single-key join, or the build side being too large for the bloom size gate. Worth checking.
